transcript.text: Our Henry has gone a bit weak and sounds rough, sort of rattly growl instead of the normal hum. It's about 12 years old. Bags and filter are new. Worth fixing?

Yes, at twelve years old Henry is still worth fixing as they are built to last. Since you have already replaced the bag and filter with no improvement, the issue likely lies in a blockage or a worn internal component like the motor bearings. To help me identify the correct spare part for your specific model, could you please provide the make and full model number? This label is usually found on the body of the vacuum, often located under the bin or near the battery compartment. If you cannot reach it right now, that is fine and we can wait until you are able to check.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
It's a Numatic Henry. I looked at the label on the bottom and it says HVR 200-22.

Thanks for confirming the model as HVR 200-22. With fresh bags and filters in place, that rough rattly growl usually points to either a blockage or worn motor bearings. To separate these causes safely, please switch off and unplug the vacuum first. Then detach the hose from the body inlet and look through it with a torch to check for any hidden clogs. Let me know if you find anything inside or if it looks clear.
[Helpful to see: image "Poor suction — what to check first" — Lost suction is usually a full bin, a dirty filter or a blockage in the hose, tube or floor head — check and clear those before suspecting the motor. Switch off and unplug first. Typical layout — your model may differ.]
I've done that and the hose is clear; a coin dropped straight through it. Suction is weak both at the end of the hose and at the head. What should I check next?

The next thing to check is whether something has jammed inside the floorhead itself. With the vacuum switched off and unplugged, turn the head over and look at the brush bar for any hair or thread wrapped around it. You can also try spinning the brush by hand to see if it moves freely or feels stuck. This will help us determine if a blockage in the floorhead is causing that rough sound and weak suction.
The Henry is a cylinder vacuum, so I'm not sure there is a brush bar on it. The floor head is just a plain one as far as I can tell. Is there anything else I should look at?

Yes, there are still a couple of safe things you can look at. Since the hose and filters are clear, the next most common cause for a rough sound on a plain head is something caught in the inlet or the floorhead itself. Please switch off and unplug the vacuum, then check the inlet where the hose connects to the body for any large debris like coins or keys. Also look inside the neck of the plain floorhead with a torch to see if anything is stuck there. Let me know what you find in either spot.

I'm afraid I can't tell that I've found anything in the inlet or the head, and suction is weak even at the end of the hose, so I doubt it's the head. I should have mentioned that after about five minutes there is a hot, burning electrical smell, and when I looked at the grille on top in the dim hall I saw sparks flickering inside. Is that important?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Yes, that is very important as sparks and a burning smell indicate an active electrical fault. You must stop using the vacuum immediately until a qualified engineer has checked it. The rattling sound combined with these signs suggests the motor bearings are worn or the internal wiring is damaged. Because of the safety risk, I cannot suggest any further checks to make it safe for you to use. Please take it to a professional repair service as soon as possible.
